sphere_commentary.overview:
All three series demonstrate credible positive listener responses with an overall mean of 6.82, though substantial variability indicates strong potential for listener-protocol matching refinement.
• HEALING shows the most consistent outcomes across entry points with strong confidence tiers
• THRIVING exhibits slightly higher mean scores, particularly in Focus & Clarity HOLD protocols
• TRANSFORMING carries the highest variance as expected for ascending-arc designs targeting low-affect states
• YouTube reach is minimal across all protocols (2-30 views) with no retention data, limiting engagement analysis
• AutoGluon identifies video engagement metrics as the strongest predictor of outcome scores
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
The three series show distinct efficacy profiles aligned with their design intent.
• HEALING leads in listener consistency with the lowest variance across entry points and strongest confidence tiers at n≥50
• THRIVING shows the highest mean scores, particularly T-FC-L3 (7.63) in Focus & Clarity HOLD protocols
• TRANSFORMING exhibits the greatest spread, reflecting ascending-arc complexity and lower-affect target populations
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols display distributional or performance anomalies warranting investigation.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10, mean=5.7, std=2.45): Significantly lower mean with high variance suggests potential protocol-listener mismatch or design issue
• H-CR-L1/L2/L3 crisis protocols: Lower means (6.35-6.52) are structurally expected but H-CR-L3 shows bimodal tendency
• T-MB-L2 (n=22, std=2.03): High standard deviation indicates response inconsistency across listener types
• X-MD-L1 (n=22, pct_pos=45%): Low positive response rate despite moderate mean suggests polarized outcomes
• Embedding drift across all protocols (<0.85 similarity) indicates rapidly evolving model representations
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Convergent signals point to specific protocol refinements and routing adjustments.
• H-CR-L3 (n=27): Bimodal distribution suggests distinct sub-group responses — investigate listener type breakdown and qualitative data to inform L2 variant for specific crisis states
• T-MB-L2 (n=22): High standard deviation (2.03) indicates response inconsistency — adjust adviser routing to manage expectations before protocol initiation
• X-MC-L3 (n=10): Low mean (5.7) and high standard deviation warrants substantial protocol redesign — consider adding introductory phase to better prepare listeners
• T-FC-L3 (n=35, mean=7.63): Peak performer in Focus & Clarity — create L4 variant to test ceiling effect and scale promotion
• H-OS-L1 (n=95, mean=7.15): Strongest efficacy with largest HEALING sample — increase promotional placement to capture undiscovered audience
• X-MD-L1 (n=22, pct_pos=45%): Low positive rate despite moderate mean — adjust rhythm architecture and investigate hold phase for ASCENT entrainment
• H-AX-L2 (n=48): Mixed listener responses — investigate split in listener types and activity modes to understand underlying patterns
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis: Cross-run drift analysis reveals all 30 protocols show similarity scores below 0.85 (range 0.507-0.821), indicating the embedding model's representation of each protocol is evolving rapidly across analysis runs. This suggests either genuine shifts in response patterns as data accumulates, or instability in the semantic encoding. No cross-protocol semantic clusters could be formed due to insufficient protocol-level embedding history. Confidence in embedding-derived insights remains low until run history deepens and cluster analysis becomes viable.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Most listeners feel noticeably better after Meadow, often within 5-10 minutes. The music and rhythm are widely liked, and it works whether you're listening for yourself or supporting someone else. It's one of the most reliable protocols for anxiety and stress.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: Cottage helps with anxiety for most people, though experiences vary more than with Meadow. Some settle quickly, others take 20 minutes. The rhythm feels balanced but the music gets mixed reviews — some love it, others find it just okay.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Valley works well especially for people supporting others through anxiety. Improvements tend to show up around 10 minutes in. The rhythm feels very settling, though the music doesn't grab everyone the same way.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Anchor helps in acute distress — people report real improvement even when they start in a bad place. Settling takes 5-10 minutes. The rhythm feels calming and balanced. It's built for crisis, so lower scores are expected, but the qualitative feedback is encouraging.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Harbor shows similar crisis support to Anchor. Some feel moderate improvement, others noticeable. Settling time varies. The music splits opinions — some love it, some feel neutral. The rhythm stays calming.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Horizon works fast for some — immediate or 5-minute settling with noticeable improvement. But the music polarizes people. It may suit a specific type of crisis state better than others.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: Pebble is the standout for overstimulation — the most responses, highest confidence, and people consistently feel better within 10 minutes whether driving, working, or relaxing. The music is genuinely liked. It's the strongest signal in the HEALING series.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Rainfall mirrors Pebble closely — noticeable improvement, 5-10 minute settling, music and rhythm well received. Slightly lower scores but same reliable pattern for sensory overwhelm.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Glacier feels the most consistent of the three overstimulation protocols — tight score clustering, noticeable improvement, balanced rhythm. It may offer the smoothest entrainment for sensory regulation.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: Lantern helps sleep reliably — most feel improvement within 10 minutes, music is loved, rhythm feels settling. It performs strongly even though the model's understanding of it keeps shifting.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Hammock works for sleep but takes longer to settle (10-20 minutes) and the music gets neutral-to-liked reactions. The rhythm feels balanced but less comforting than Lantern or Midnight.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Midnight supports sleep with 5-10 minute settling and noticeable improvement. Music opinion splits, rhythm feels balanced. Consistent performer across the sleep trio.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Ember gives a modest creative lift. Some feel it right away, others at 10 minutes. Music and rhythm are liked but it's the weakest of the three Creative Flow protocols.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: Current improves slightly on Ember — more people report meaningful improvement, used during commutes and sleep. Music is loved by those who respond. A small groove refinement makes a difference.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Aurora scores highest for Creative Flow but with few responses. Those who try it report noticeable to significant improvement during sleep and work. Music opinion splits. Promising but needs more listeners.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Compass gives moderate focus support but the rhythm feels slightly busy to many. Improvement shows up around 5 minutes during study or relaxation. It's the least effective Focus protocol.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: Waypoint works better for focus — 10-minute settling, strong improvement reports during caregiving and therapy. Rhythm feels balanced. A solid mid-range option.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: Summit is the peak focus protocol — the highest scores, most significant improvements, 10-minute settling, music widely loved. But scores split into two groups, suggesting it works exceptionally for some and less for others.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Stone supports maintenance and balance well but takes 20 minutes to settle. Music splits neutral/liked. Good outcome with slow entrainment — may need an earlier engagement hook.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Axis shows inconsistent results — some settle in 5 minutes, others take 10, with mixed improvement ratings. Music and rhythm opinions vary. Best suited with managed expectations about timing.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Orbit shows promise for maintenance with quick 5-minute settling during study and caregiving. Music liked by most. But very few responses so far — needs more real-world testing.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Cavern helps clarify the mind for about half the listeners, settling in 5-10 minutes. The music and rhythm are genuinely loved — very settling. The model predicts it could work even better for the right people.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Starlight feels similar to Cavern but with fewer responses. Those who try it report strong improvement, immediate or 10-minute settling, and love the music and rhythm. Model favors this as the optimal mind-clarity option.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Cosmos struggles — the lowest scores in the library, high variability, and mixed music/rhythm reactions. It may ask too much too soon. Needs a gentler entry phase to prepare listeners.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Footpath gives moderate motivation support but only 45% report positive change despite a decent average. The model predicts much higher efficacy for the right subgroup. The ascending rhythm may not catch everyone.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: Trail shows similar challenges to Footpath — low positive rate, 20-minute settling for some. Music is loved by responders but neutral for others. The ASCENT design struggles to lift motivation consistently.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Switchback scores highest for motivation but with wild variance — it either works very well or not much. Quick settling for responders. There's likely a specific subgroup this fits perfectly.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: Breeze supports mood and energy with moderate scores but the model predicts it's the top protocol for low-affect states. It cross-helps anxiety and crisis too. Music loved, rhythm balanced. An undiscovered gem for the right listeners.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Sunrise mirrors Breeze closely — consistent mood/energy support, 20-minute or immediate settling, music and rhythm well liked. The model sees it helping anxiety, crisis, and motivation too. But its analytical profile keeps shifting.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Updraft is the weakest of the Mood trio with fewer responses. It has potential but needs more listeners to find its footing. Marketing focus could unlock better data.
